chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

When four qualities are gathered for the food, it is complete: when it is lawful, when many hands partake of it, when the name of God, the Blessed and Exalted, is mentioned at its beginning, and when He is praised at its end.
ai.seo_question: What are the four conditions that make a meal complete according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* via the chain of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, this hadith establishes a holistic framework for sustenance that bridges individual piety with communal solidarity. By requiring the food to be halal, abundant enough for many hands, and framed by the invocation and praise of God, it transforms a mundane act of eating into a spiritual practice that reinforces social bonds and divine gratitude.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-39 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Muqayrih, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Muslim al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
If food has the following four characteristics it is complete: It is lawful; many people eat it; it is eaten by mentioning the Blessed the Sublime God’s name; and God is praised after it is eaten.”
